title: New wrap-bound rejection row is green vacuously — balance validation never runs
evidence:
core/catalog_test.odin:887:
		{"box interval over the wrap bound", replace1(BAL_VALID, `"dot_interval_ticks": 2400`, `"dot_interval_ticks": 1099511627776`, 1), "must be <= 2^40 (the HUD permille math's wrap bound)"},
--- check_reject_balance sources literal (1001-1008) sets node_types/pipe_tiers/balance/packet_types/demand/eras but NO crises field:
	src := Catalog_Sources{
		node_types   = transmute([]u8)string(NT_VALID),
		pipe_tiers   = transmute([]u8)string(TIER_VALID),
		balance      = transmute([]u8)bal,
		packet_types = transmute([]u8)string(PKT_VALID),
		demand       = transmute([]u8)string(DEM_VALID),
		eras       = transmute([]u8)string(ERAS_VALID),
	}
--- then (1010-1013):
	cerr := catalogs_load(cat, &src)
	if cerr.file != "balance.json" {
		testing.expectf(t, cerr.file != "", "expected a balance.json rejection (rule %q), got %q %q", want_rule, cerr.file, cerr.rule)
		return
	}
--- core/catalog.odin:745-746 (crises parsed BEFORE the box block at 1153, nil doc fails):
		v, e := json.parse(src.crises, parse_integers = true)
		if e != nil { return {"crises.json", "$", "invalid JSON"} }
detail: catalogs_load fails earlier at crises.json (nil doc); the helper accepts any non-empty error file and returns, so the row is green without exercising the 2^40 guard. Probe-verified: deleting the wrap-bound branch keeps core 298/298 green.
recommended_fix: Add crises = transmute([]u8)string(CRISES_VALID) to check_reject_balance's Catalog_Sources so the balance.json validator actually runs for every bal_rows row.

title: The 2^40 wrap-bound branch is unreachable — the row's expected rule can never be produced
detail: jint_strict bounds di to i32 (max 2^31-1 < 2^40), so this branch is dead code. Probe with the crises doc fixed: 1099511627776 rejects with rule "clock keys must be integers (no decimals)", never the expected wrap-bound rule — the row cannot pass as written.
recommended_fix: Validate the raw JSON integer against 2^40 before the i32 narrowing (i64-tolerant parse), or pin the actual "clock keys must be integers" rejection in the test row.

title: dots_post_crisis measures 'after first crisis onset', not 'after the last crisis resolved'
evidence:
harness/econ.odin:43:
	dots_post_crisis: i32, // dots AFTER the last crisis resolved (the no-death-spiral recovery)
harness/econ.odin:90:
				if stats.saw_crisis_active do stats.dots_post_crisis += 1
harness/econ.odin:94:
		if len(s.crisis.active) > 0 do stats.saw_crisis_active = true
detail: saw_crisis_active latches at first onset and never resets on resolve, so dots DURING the crisis count — 'after the last crisis resolved' is not measured and the recovery leg is weaker than the r1 W3 claim ('dots land after the crisis').
recommended_fix: Clear the latch when crisis.active empties so only true post-resolution dots count, or reword the comment and FAIL message to 'after the first crisis onset'.

evidence:

detail: The ruling-1 start-era change makes era-1/2 demand live first-play content while the data doc still says the app runs era 3 from tick 1 and their re-tune is deferred — a spec-vs-data contradiction the delta created.
